summary: A grand, symmetrical fortress or mansion featuring a two-story main body flanked by tall, square towers. The structure is built primarily with end stone walls, accented by stone brick pillars and horizontal bands of wood and white blocks. The central building has a brick roof, while the towers feature flat, overhanging caps. The entire structure appears to sit on a slightly elevated or overhanging base.

shape.overall_form: Central rectangular block with tall flanking towers

materials.name: stonebrick
materials.role: tower corners, base support, roof accents

rebuild_hints: Begin with the base, creating an overhang using stone bricks and a trim of white blocks (likely quartz).
Construct the main two-story body using end stone, separating the first and second floors with a horizontal band of wood planks and white blocks.
Build the tall towers on the flanks using end stone for the faces and stone bricks for the corner pillars.
Cap the towers with flat, overhanging roofs made of stone brick slabs/blocks and a layer of bricks.
Construct a stepped or gabled brick roof over the central section of the building.
Incorporate glowstone for lighting, as indicated by the close-up details.
uncertainties: The exact depth of the building is difficult to determine precisely from the exterior angles provided.
The specific type of white block used for the trim and banding (e.g., quartz, white concrete, or snow) is uncertain.
The interior layout and the exact placement of the glowstone blocks shown in the close-up images are unknown.
